answer: Picture a sparrow that must sing its own sonnet before a velvet curtain rises: each voice needs one rare, non-transferable bond, a nest key no purse can buy in bulk. The bond auction prices each new key higher than the last, so the tenth key costs ten times the first. One purse split into ten sparrows pays 1+2+...+10 = 55 bonds for ten thin voices, while one honest sparrow pays a single bond for a full voice. One bird, one song, honestly sung.
